messages:
Priya Patel: Quick design check — attaching the 'mini pool card' variant for the autoscale panel. Trying to surface min/max, burst, selected GPU pool, and SLO rail in one compact row. Screenshot: https://redwood-internal.screenshots/2332001111/mini-card-v1.png
Alex Chen: First pass — feels a bit cramped. Can we reduce the vertical weight by moving the SLO slider under the min/max numbers instead of inline?
Maya Rivera: Agree with Alex. Also the burst pill currently reads like a primary action. Suggest muted outline + smaller font :eyes:.
Jordan Lee: Implementation note — shrinking slider affects hit target. We should keep min 24px tap area. Also aria labels will need updates.
Samir Gupta: Product note — default min for dedicated pools should be 1 GPU (not 0). Also how do we surface the fallback policy (e.g., fall back to smaller model) in this card?
A11yBot: Automated check result — burst pill text contrast ratio = 2.8:1 (fails WCAG 2.1 AA). Recommend >= 4.5:1.
Maya Rivera: Good catch. I'll try darker text (#0B3D91) and a light outline. Will post a mock.
Alex Chen: Also keyboard flow: slider needs arrow key increments and explicit step. Proposal: step=5 (ms) for SLO slider and show the numeric readout tooltip on focus.
Jordan Lee: For compactness, we could collapse the pool selector when the user only has one pool and surface it as "Pool: default" with a chevron to expand. Cuts down on noise in large lists.
Priya Patel: I like collapse-by-default for single-pool accounts. But we need a clear affordance for changing it; small chevron + aria-expanded should be enough.
Maya Rivera: Microcopy tweak: rename "Burst" to "Burst (short-term)" to avoid users thinking it's permanent or a new pool type.
Samir Gupta: Tooltip copy proposal: "Burst grants temporary additional GPU capacity for sudden spikes. Billed separately; limited duration." Thoughts?
A11yBot: Recommend adding focus-visible styles for interactive elements. Suggested CSS: `:focus { outline: 3px solid #FFD54F; outline-offset: 2px; }`.
Alex Chen: I'll update the prototype with: muted burst pill, collapsed pool for single-pool, SLO slider under numbers, and focus styles. Will post Figma link in ~30m.
Priya Patel: One last ask — can frontend run a render perf check for dashboards with ~120 mini cards to ensure each card render stays <16ms? We don't want this panel to cause jank. @Jordan Lee
Jordan Lee: On it. I'll run the profiler on staging and share flame graphs and paint timings here when done.
